# E0002: unexpected character

Outside strings and comments, Stilt reads only ASCII, so a curly quote or a symbol pasted from a document isn't code. Retype it, or put it inside a string.

- Rule: [`lexical.whitespace`](../../reference/02-lexical.md#lexical.whitespace)
- Reported at: the unexpected character.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `syntax` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0002:2
fn main() / io {
  print(“hello”)
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
fn main() / io {
  print("hello")
}
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0002_backtick_string.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0002_backtick_string.lt):

```text
── UNEXPECTED CHARACTER ────────────────── E0002_backtick_string.lt:3:9  [E0002]

Stilt writes a string in double quotes, and inserts a value as `{name}`:

  3 │   print(`hello ${name}`)
    │         ^

Every string inserts the value of each `{…}` in it, as `"hello {name}"`.

To fix it, write it in double quotes:

  3 │   print("hello {name}")
    │         ~      ~     ~
```

`stilt check` on [`E0002_unexpected_character.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0002_unexpected_character.lt):

```text
── UNEXPECTED CHARACTER ───────────── E0002_unexpected_character.lt:2:9  [E0002]

Unexpected character U+201C:

  2 │   print(“hello”)
    │         ^

Outside strings and comments, Stilt reads only ASCII, so a curly quote or a
symbol pasted from a document isn't code. Retype it, or put it inside a string.
```
